sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial skeleton with dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ribs, shoulder bones, a forearm bone, a hand claw, hip bones, leg bones, ankle bones, and a toe bone.

Paul Barrett and colleagues formally described the species as a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaur in 2026 after finding the holotype in March 2018 on the margin of Lake Kariba by a South African and Zimbabwean-led expedition. The specimen is housed in the Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo under the accession code NHMZ 2583. The genus name Musango honors the Musango Archosaur Site near the Musango Safari Camp on Lake Kariba where the fossil was found, while the species name matusadonaensis refers to the nearby Matusadona National Park. Musango is the fifth dinosaur genus described from Zimbabwe.

Based on comparisons with more complete relatives, researchers suggest Musango was likely an obligate biped. Estimates based on the holotype suggest the animal reached a body length of about 4.5 meters and a mass of about 222 kilograms.
Musango is classified as a sauropodomorph belonging to the family Unaysauridae. Phylogenetic analysis places Musango in the clade Unaysauridae as the sister taxon to Musankwa.
The animal lived during the Late Triassic epoch, specifically the Norian age, in the Upper Triassic (Norian) in the Pebbly Arkose Formation of Zimbabwe.
